title: fix(app-shell): a related-list row form action opens the clicked row, not a blank create form
body:
Fixes #13063
Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

A `type: 'form'` action placed at `record_related` and fired from a related-list row ("Log Time" on a project's Tasks list) opened the declared form as a blank CREATE form for the child object. `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`'s `runRowAction` retargeted the row action through the DEFINITION only (`objectName`, `recordId`, `params._rowRecord`) and ran it on the page's shared runner. `executeForm` reads the record and its object from the runner context only, and that context names the parent page. It ignores `action.objectName` on purpose (objectui#4292). So `crossesObjectBoundary('task.edit', 'project')` answered true and the runner navigated to the bare `/forms/NAME`.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/core` `ActionRunner.execute(action, callContext?)`.** The runner had no per-call context path: `execute` took the action only, and the context changed only through `updateContext`, which mutates the shared runner. So this adds an optional second parameter to the existing method (no new export). With `callContext`, the dispatch runs on a one-shot runner over `{ ...context, ...callContext }`. That runner shares the original's handlers, scripts, confirm, toast, modal, navigation, param-collection and result-dialog handlers, and its translator. The runner's own context is not touched. Two keys follow the merge:
  - `ctx`, the `ActionProvider` mirror, so `${ctx.record.…}` reads the same record as `${record.…}`;
  - `objectFields` / `objectActions`. When `callContext` names another object and brings none of its own, the base pair is dropped, so the page object's definitions never answer for the child's record. That is what a retargeted action already got from `readContextObjectFields` / `readContextObjectActions`, which answer only for the context's own `objectName`.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`.** A row dispatch hands the clicked row as its execution context, `{ record: row, objectName: CHILD }`, through `useAction().runner.execute(def, rowContext)`. The definition keeps `objectName`, `recordId` and `_rowRecord`, because the `api` / `flow` / `script` handlers and the update path read them. A toolbar dispatch (no row) keeps the page context exactly as before.
- `executeForm` is unchanged and still ignores `action.objectName` (objectui#4292).

## Other row-action types, measured by reading the dispatch path on `origin/main` 083e807358

| type | where it reads the row and the object | after this change |
|---|---|---|
| `update` (`operation: 'update'`) | `action.objectName`, then the context. Row from `params._rowRecord`. Field map and declared `patch` answer only for the context's object | same row and object. Field map and declarations are `undefined`, as before (dropped instead of mismatched) |
| `api` | registered handler (record page and console runtime): `_rowRecord`, `action.objectName`, `action.recordId` from the definition | unchanged. Pinned: the clicked row on the definition, and the row in the handler's context argument |
| `flow` / `script` | registered handler: `resolveServerActionRecordId` reads `params.recordId`, then `_rowRecord`, before any context. Object is `action.objectName` first | unchanged |
| `url` / `navigation` | builtin. Target templates evaluate against the runner context (`${record.…}`, `${ctx.recordId}`) | **now the row**. Before, a row's `url` template read the PARENT record. This is the ruling's one sanctioned change: a `record_related` row action sees the row as its context |
| `form` | builtin `executeForm`: context only | **the defect, now the row** |

## Pins

New `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.rowFormContext-13063.test.tsx`. It mounts the real `ActionProvider` with the record page's context shape, the real bridge, the `record:related_list` renderer and the runner's own `form` executor.
- (a) "Log Time" from the row navigates to `/forms/task.edit?recordId=t1&recordObject=task`.
- (b) controls:
  - the same action from the child's record page gives the same URL;
  - a page-level form action on the parent still opens `?recordId=P-1&recordObject=project`, after a row dispatch too, so no context leaks onto the shared runner. A page-level action at a child view still stays a create;
  - the `api` row action (`archive`) reaches its handler with `objectName: task`, `recordId: t1`, `_rowRecord: row` on the definition.

New `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/ActionRunner.callContext-13063.test.ts` covers:
- the merge, and that it is one-shot;
- shared handlers and confirm;
- the identity alias surviving;
- the `ctx` mirror following the merge;
- the object-definition pair being dropped for another object and kept for the same one.

## Ablation: the row back on the definition only

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack checkout) replaced `runner.execute(def as ActionDef, rowContext)` with `runner.execute(def as ActionDef)` in the bridge. Result: anchor x1 to x0, blob `84152195036a` to `c1ce37eefa57`.
- The pin file went `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`.
- (a) failed with `Received "/forms/task.edit"`, the defect's bare create URL.
- The `api` control failed only on its context assertion (`objectName: "project"`, `record.id: "P-1"`); its definition assertions held.
- The two other controls stayed green.
- Restore: `blob after restore 84152195036a… == blob at HEAD 84152195036a…`, and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

## Verification (head 3dafcd4657)

- Union vitest (`--maxWorkers=1`): 52 files, `Test Files 52 passed (52)` / `Tests 604 passed (604)`. The set is the two new pins, every test file naming `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, every `ActionRunner*.test.ts` in core, and `packages/react/src/context/__tests__`.
- Closure build `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`: exit 0. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check && pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 4 changed TS/TSX files: 0 errors. Warning counts equal base on both source files (core 12, app-shell 13). Type-aware linting is off (`--print-config` shows no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so these edits cannot move any verdict on a file they do not touch.
- Lock-free battery, every one exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`, `new-line-citations`, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-presence`.
- `check:spec-floors`: exit 1, `no-artifact`. It needs a whole-workspace build; recorded, not fixed.
- Declared to CI: the full `packages/core/` and `packages/app-shell/` test directories.

## Acceptance notes

- The bridge calls `useAction().runner.execute` rather than the provider's `execute`, because the provider's wrapper takes one argument and `@object-ui/react` is outside this card's file surface. The wrapper's `loading` / `error` / `result` state is not set for related-row dispatches. Measured: no `useAction()` consumer in `packages/` or `apps/` reads those three fields. An optional second argument on `ActionProvider`'s `execute` would let the bridge go back through the wrapper. Carrier: none.
- `url` row templates now bind the row (table above). It is the sanctioned change, so no separate pin was added; the `form` pin covers the context path both executors read.
